topic.name: The Range of a Transformed Radical Function

question.explanation:
The range of $y = \sqrt[7] x$ is $ y \in (-\infty,\infty). $

Transformations do not change this interval. Therefore, the range of $f(x)$ is $y \in (-\infty,\infty).$

example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Odd Index

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt[6] x$ is

\[ \sqrt[6] x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt[6]{4-3x} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-4$ and then adding $2,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt[6]{4-3x} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] -4\sqrt[6]{4-3x} &\le 0 \\[3pt] -4\sqrt[6]{4-3x}+2 &\le 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in (-\infty,2].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

example.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index

question.explanation:
The range of $\sqrt[4] x$ is

\[ \sqrt[4] x \ge 0. \]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Hence,

\[ \sqrt[4]{2x-7} \ge 0. \]

Multiplying the above inequality by $-3$ and then adding $2,$ we get

\begin{align*} \sqrt[4]{2x-7} &\ge 0 \\[3pt] -3\sqrt[4]{2x-7} &\le 0 \\[3pt] -3\sqrt[4]{2x-7}+2 &\le 2. \end{align*}

Therefore, the range of the given function is $f(x) \in (-\infty,2].$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
